turns.text: also, more sprites: in a subagent, anything that could work nicely for the welcome hall?  also, anything that could work nicely for a level outisde the hall, a furutistic (think, 2032 singularity?) parking lot? We enter via the main gate like all other bots, and walk casually until we reach the welcome hall? then we start fighting, then we go into the first elevator?

items.text:
Love the arc — gate → parking lot → walk in "casually" among the other bots → welcome hall → it turns → first elevator. That's a proper cold open (floor 00), and it wants its own two prop families. I'll spin the sprite agent on it — with one sequencing note: the props agent is currently inside src/props.rs fixing the flicker/motes/wash, so I'll launch the sprite agent the moment that one reports (minutes), to avoid two agents in the same file. Its brief, so you can adjust now if you want:

Parking lot / gate (2032 singularity, outdoor, night): autonomous cars in bays (a couple of body types, hazard/charging LEDs, one with doors open), inductive charging pads with pulsing rings, the main gate (barrier arms, scanner posts, a guard booth with a screen), bollards, planters/shrubs, lamp posts casting light pools, road markings/arrows, a delivery drone pad (drone landed), a stack of crates/pallets, a bike/scooter rack, drainage grate, a big holo billboard (the datacenter's logo/slogan), queue of "other bots" props (idle robot silhouettes? — those should be actual rogues walking calmly, scenario, not props).

Welcome hall: reception desk with a receptionist bot terminal, turnstiles/security scanner arch, waiting benches, potted plants, a big lobby holo-screen (welcome message, "please queue"), directory totem, vending machine, coffee corner, coat/charging lockers, floor logo inlay, elevator lobby with call panel (the first elevator!), velvet ropes/queue posts, a security camera (exists), a fire extinguisher, an ATM-like "credit terminal".

Style rules: same as the existing library — top-down, front face at +y with LEDs, top-left light and drop shadows, layered (before/after), animated where it helps (charging rings, barrier arm sway, billboard scroll, coffee steam), consistent palette. Then, once the props exist, floor 00's level + scenario (walk in unchallenged, the hall, the turn) is the natural next content step — the editor + scenario format can already do "enter zone → dialogue → spawn wave → open exit".

Say if you want any of that changed; otherwise it goes as-is right after the current agent lands.

turns.text: the check-e2e is slow.... do we have 2 systems, one running the engine part only in fake mode and one running the whole e2e thing? also, how does the editor work?

items.text:
Yes to both, and the slowness has a specific cause.

Two test systems
1. Headless engine gate — tests/playthrough_gate.rs drives src/sim.rs: the real ECS systems (movement, AI, combat, bullets, pickups…) in a native Rust loop with a scripted bot player, no browser, no rendering, no wasm. Runs in make check-test in ~0.5 s per floor. Its known limit: it doesn't run the scenario/elevator systems yet, so its "win" is still kill-all — a smoke test, not the real completion path.
2. Full e2e — make check-e2e: rebuilds the wasm in release (LTO), installs bun deps, starts a server, runs Playwright/Chromium with SwiftShader software WebGL (3 specs, ~30–40 s). The slow part is almost never the tests: it's the release wasm rebuild (minutes when the cache is cold, and much worse when 2–3 agents' cargo builds fight over target/, which is what happened tonight). Two cheap speedups if you want them: make the wasm build a proper Make dependency (skip when nothing under src/ changed), and a make e2e-only target that just runs bunx playwright test against the already-built wasm.

How the editor works
- tools/levels.html + levels-editor.js / -format.js / -diff.js is a plain vanilla-JS app (no build step) served by serve.py; ?viz → LEVELS just iframes it.
- It reads levels/index.json and levels/floor_NN.json over HTTP; the canvas is the floor plan (walls/rooms/zones/spawns/pickups/entry/exits), the right panel is meta + the scenario steps; everything is validated against docs/SCENARIO_FORMAT.md (ids, references, to, speakers).
- SAVE = PUT /levels/floor_NN.json with the X-Editor-Token header; serve.py checks the token + path allowlist, writes the file atomically and upserts index.json. COPY DIFF gives a patch -p1 diff to paste to me instead.
- The game doesn't read JSON at runtime: make gen-levels runs tools/gen_levels.py (stdlib only) which validates and generates src/levels_data.rs (static Rust data) → rebuild wasm → the floors are compiled in. make verify includes check-levels so JSON and generated Rust can't drift. Props follow the same shape: props/props.json → gen_props.py → src/props_data.rs.

So the loop is: edit in the browser → SAVE (or paste diff) → make gen-levels → make build-wasm → play. If you'd like, I can add a "regen on save" hook to serve.py (run gen_levels.py/gen_props.py after a successful PUT) so the only manual step left is the wasm rebuild.

turns.text: could we decide to not use the check-e2e in our regular dev loop, only before the final commit?...   ;    could the editor be part of the rust thing instead of a web app?.... WDYT?   ;

items.text:
1. E2E only before commits — yes, agreed, and I'll enforce it. make verify (fmt, host+wasm clippy, unit + integration + the headless sim gate, release/wasm build, levels/props checks) is the dev-loop gate; make check-e2e runs once at commit points (and in CI). I've been telling every agent to run e2e — that's a big part of why the loop felt slow (each e2e = a cold LTO wasm rebuild, times three agents contending). From now on agents get: make verify + a targeted headless screenshot of what they changed; e2e is mine, at the end. I'll tell the running sprite agent now.

2. Editor in Rust instead of a web app — WDYT: yes, in phases, and the reasons matter.

Why yes:
- WYSIWYG. The ?viz toolbox is already wasm-drawn (tracker, gallery, props inspector, effects) — the LEVELS tab is the odd iframe out. A native editor draws the floor with the real renderer: real walls/floor, real props at their pixel grid, robots, elevators, even scenario preview with the actual comms panel. The HTML canvas is a re-implementation that will always drift from the game's look.
- One source of truth for the format. Today the schema lives three times: gen_levels.py, levels-editor-format.js, and the Rust runtime — speaker lists, sfx names, trigger kinds already had to be synced by hand (and were out of sync once). In Rust it's one definition + one validator, and the editor can't produce data the game can't load.
- Prop placement (the missing link) needs a canvas tool anyway; building it in the wasm editor makes it free for the game to render identically.

Costs, honestly:
- Immediate-mode UI in a canvas: text fields (dialogue lines!), dropdowns, scroll lists, drag/resize handles — the web app got those free from HTML. We have viz_button and keyboard capture; a text-field widget + a list widget is maybe a day of careful work, not more.
- Saving still needs a JS bridge (wasm can't write files) — that already exists (vizSaveProps / the PUT API), and the JSON→levels_data.rs generation stays unless we hand-write a tiny JSON reader in Rust for editor mode (no serde by rule; ~200 lines; fine).

How I'd sequence it:
1. Now-ish (with prop placement): the LEVELS tab becomes native for the spatial part — walls, zones, elevators, spawns, pickups, and props placed over the real rendered floor with the real renderer, snapping to the pixel grid, live animation, camera pan/zoom, undo. The scenario text/steps stay in the HTML panel for the moment (side by side, not iframe-of-everything).
2. Then: port the scenario forms (steps, triggers, dialogue with a text widget, comms preview using the real render_comms) into wasm and delete tools/levels*.js/html — one ?viz, one language, one format.

So: not a rewrite for its own sake — the WYSIWYG + single-format arguments are strong enough that I'd start phase 1 as soon as the sprite drop lands, since prop placement has to be built somewhere anyway. Want that as the next task after the sprites?

items.text:
Started, in its own worktree with today's full state (shared cargo cache, no e2e in its loop). Its scope, end to end:

- Format: floors get props: [{kind, x, y, rot, size}] → gen_levels.py validates against PROP_NAMES → FloorDef.props; the HTML editor round-trips the field untouched.
- Game: placed props rendered in-game with each prop's saved pixel grid, under actors — the missing link between the library and the levels (decoration only in phase 1).
- Native editor in the LEVELS tab: the floor drawn with the real renderer (props animating live), pan/zoom/fit, grid+snap, tools for walls/rooms/zones/spawns/pickups/entry/exits and a prop palette (place, R rotate, resize, nudge, delete), select/move/resize, undo/redo, minimal text widget for ids/labels, validation, SAVE via a vizSaveLevel bridge (same token flow) — with a "SCENARIO (web)" button that opens the old HTML panel for the steps/dialogue until phase 2 ports those too.

Merge plan when both agents land: sprites (main tree, props.rs/lib.rs/props.json) and editor (worktree, editor*.rs new + small lib.rs hooks + scenario.rs/gen_levels.py/format) — I have the base snapshot for a proper 3-way merge, then make verify, one e2e, screenshots.

turns.text: do you think you'd be able to craft level 0 yourself? with pauses at the right times, etc?   is there anything missing now that you could work on in autonomy ?

items.text:
Yes — I can author it end to end (layout, props, the other bots' behaviour, the beats and pauses, dialogue) once three engine pieces exist, and those are exactly the autonomous work worth doing now. What's missing, concretely:

Engine features floor 0 needs (none exist yet):
1. Passive bots — today every rogue is hostile from spawn. The cold open needs bots that walk to the hall like you do and ignore you: an AI mode Passive { walk_to: zone } (queue up, idle-fidget), flipped to hostile by a scenario action alert (all / a spawn group) — that's "the turn".
2. Beats/pauses — a hold action (lock player input for N s while a beat plays: the gate scan, the receptionist exchange, the CORRUPTOR breaking through the lobby holo) and a move hint for the player-guided camera; plus a wait_for_comms gating so exits open only after the feed idles.
3. Floor surface styles — floors are all the same checker; the lot needs asphalt/markings, the hall marble/tiles: a floor.surface field (palette + tile pattern) → generator → level.render.
4. Prop placement — in progress (editor agent).
5. Small: exits that read as doors not lifts (label/style flag), a floor-0 slot in the index/lore ("00 — GATE / PARKING", entry = the main gate, exit = MAIN DOORS → floor 1), and floor 1 becomes the lobby proper (turnstiles, desk, the turn, then the first elevator).

Then the authoring (mine, in JSON via the format — no agent needed): the walk from the gate past charging cars, billboard and lamp pools with 4–6 passive bots drifting toward the doors; scanner-arch beat at the gate (hold 2 s, "ACCESS GRANTED"); doors open; floor 1: queue at the turnstiles, receptionist line, the CORRUPTOR through the lobby holo → alert → fight → SERVICE LIFT opens; comms lines in LORE voice throughout.

I'll start 1–3 + 5 now, in a second worktree from the same base snapshot (so both agents 3-way merge cleanly with the editor's format changes), and author floors 0/1 as soon as placement + these land:

items.name: Agent
items.target: Cold-open engine: passive bots, holds, floor surfaces

items.text:
Two agents now running in parallel worktrees off the same base:
- editor — native LEVELS tab + prop placement (format props, generator, in-game render, palette, save);
- cold-open engine — passive bots (type: "passive", walk_to, groups), alert / hold / look_at scenario actions, door-style exits, per-floor surface (asphalt/marble/…), floor id 0 with to: "surface" for the ending sentinel, a placeholder floor_00.json, tests.

When both land I 3-way merge them into the main tree (I kept the base snapshot), verify, and then I author floors 0 and 1 myself — layout + props from the new families, 4–6 passive bots drifting to the doors, the gate scan hold, billboard/doors look-ats, the lobby queue at the turnstiles, the receptionist beat, the CORRUPTOR through the lobby holo → alert → fight → SERVICE LIFT — with dialogue in LORE voice. Then screenshots + one e2e before you commit.

Other autonomous items I'd pick up right after (no decisions needed from you): regen-on-save in serve.py, an e2e-only Make target, the sim gate running scenarios so the headless win means "extracted", and the dedup/dead-code cleanup list.
